title: Settings
description: Composable settings host. Native general / writing / reading / discussion plus iframed permalinks / media / privacy.

documentation.purpose: Composable host that mounts a vertical nav (left) + one selected settings panel (right). Bundles seven built-in panels reflecting WordPress's settings screens: general (native), writing (native, partial REST coverage), reading (native, partial), discussion (native, partial), permalinks (iframed — no REST), media (iframed — partial REST), privacy (iframed — no REST). Shells narrow the panel set via `config.panels[]`. Unknown sub-routes fall back to the first available panel rather than 404-ing. Each sub-panel rebuilds one wp-admin screen (`docs/screens/settings-general.md`, `settings-writing.md`, `settings-reading.md`, `settings-discussion.md`, `settings-permalinks.md`, `settings-media.md`, `settings-privacy.md`); this host has no single-screen equivalent.

reads.source: Per-panel — see settings-general / settings-writing / settings-reading / settings-discussion individual app docs.
reads.purpose: Each native panel mounts its own component and reads its own slice of `useEntityRecord('root','site')` or related entities.

states.renders: Empty-state copy: `No settings panels are available.`
Two-column layout: nav on left (Item per panel) + active panel (or IframeApp) on right.

interactions.trigger: Click a panel in the nav
interactions.effect: `setActive(panel.id)`; right column re-renders with the new panel's Component (or iframe).

a11y.focus-management: Item nav handles its own focus; clicking a nav item moves focus to the activated entry.

constraints.note: Active panel id is in `useState`, NOT the URL. Refreshing the page lands on the first panel, not the previously-active one. A future iteration may move this to a URL slot for parity with NavigationApp's `?screen=` pattern.
If `config.panels` allowlist filters out every built-in panel (empty array passes through), the empty-state UI surfaces. Authoring tools should warn if the resolved list is empty.
Every built-in panel requires `manage_options`. The kernel's capability gate suppresses the whole app for users without it; per-panel cap gating is uniform today.
Permalinks, Media, and Privacy panels delegate to `IframeApp` because their settings have no REST coverage. The iframe inherits chrome-stripping CSS but iframes are otherwise opaque to the host.

design-system-leakage.purpose: Vertical nav — WPDS 0.12 has no ItemGroup port.
